summary: The Maven and Gradle plugins expose an environment parameter for adding extra environment variables.
extended_definition: The Maven and Gradle plugins expose an environment parameter for adding extra environment variables.

supporting_pages.title: "appengine-web.xml reference \_|\_ App Engine standard environment \_|\_\
evidence_snippets: For example: <staging> <delete-jsps>false</delete-jsps> </staging> Staging option defaults The defaults for staging options are different depending on whether you use Google Cloud SDK-based tooling, such as the gcloud CLI, or the Google Cloud SDK-based Maven , Gradle , or IntelliJ plugins.
Element Description <application> Not required if you deploy your app using Google Cloud SDK-based tooling, such as the gcloud app deploy command, IntelliJ plugins, Maven or Gradle plugins.
You will need to specify additional configuration parameters for each non-default service, which were formerly known as modules.

supporting_pages.title: "Java runtime environment \_|\_ App Engine standard environment \_|\_ Google\
evidence_snippets: Before you begin Download the latest version of the Google Cloud CLI or update your gcloud CLI to the current version: gcloud components update To deploy using Maven, you will need to add the App Engine Maven Plugin to your pom.xml file: <plugin> <groupId>com.google.cloud.tools</groupId> <artifactId>appengine-maven-plugin</artifactId> <version>2.8.1</version> </plugin> Other options for deploying include using the gcloud app deploy command or the App Engine Gradle plugin .
If your Maven or Gradle build file produces an executable Uber JAR, the runtime starts your application by running an Uber JAR application.
You can define additional environment variables in your app.yaml file , but the above values cannot be overridden, except for NODE ENV .
